newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end down, pushed by profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end down, pushed by profit-taking.

text.p: Tokyo stocks ended the Wednesday session on a weak note, pushed lower by profit taking in both banking-sector and some blue-chip shares in afternoon trade, brokers said. They said the market lacked direction and trade was very thin with investors staying on the sidelines.
The 225-share Nikkei average fell 79.15 points, or 0.42 percent, to close at 18,990.92. Its March futures were down 90 points at 19,030.
"The market wants to see what the U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman has to say in testimony scheduled for later today," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities.
Kyotaru was also the most heavily traded issue, with volume of 8.399 million shares. Frozen food producer Katokichi lost 10 yen to end at 1,960.
Market speculation that Toshiba Corp's group earnings for this business year may be weaker than the company expected knocked it down 17 yen to 698 yen.
Food trader Nissei Sangyo Co Ltd rose 100 yen to 1,440 after it announced it would pay a commemorative dividend for this business year, brokers said.
By sector, credit/lease, rubber, oil, communications and machinery were the main gainers.
